analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: ASML beats & looking to build more; Semis/AI sentiment is poor; VOD appeals to Brussels against Satellites; BT 14 Oct 2026
key_insights: Semis fell for a fifth straight session, nearly erasing an intraday 3.3% drop. Memory and semicap led on renewed concerns about China's CXMT and a cooling in AI bottleneck trades. MU and SNDK have fallen in seven of the past eight sessions, while PC hardware, IT services, selected software and the Mag 7 stayed firm.

ASML Q3 beat and raised. The desk says Q3 gross margin of 57.4% came before the recent price increases. ASML says 30% capacity growth in 2027 and 30% in 2028 will not meet customer demand, so it is looking at ways to extend capacity further in 2028 and beyond.

ASML Q4 2026 guidance: sales of EUR 14.2-15.2bn, 3% above VA consensus at the mid-point, and gross margin of 57% vs Street 56.7%. Implied Q4 EBIT is 7% above VA consensus. 2026 revenue guidance was raised to EUR 44-45bn from EUR 43-45bn, 1% above VA consensus at the mid-point.

ASML price increases start to show partly in 2027, with the full impact in 2028 and beyond. Early investor feedback is mixed, with some wanting more detail on the guide. The desk calls that unrealistic given ASML sells to a handful of customers.

The desk says bears are criticising the lack of a 2027 upgrade, but ASML announced a large upgrade at Q2 and more EUV machines cannot be built in one quarter. It describes investor sentiment as caught in a bearish feedback loop, with semiconductor discussions focused on who can make the most negative case.

AMAT fell 7% in a sector-wide selloff. The desk attributes this partly to disappointment over the lack of a specific medium-term WFE forecast and an earnings target before 2030, and to a gross margin guide that disappointed.

AI/semis sentiment has turned cautious on whether the AI infrastructure build-out can meet valuation expectations into 2028. Cited constraints are power access, funding cost and availability, model competition including Meta's Muse/Wonder models, and custom silicon redistributing value. Positioning is crowded, so modest doubts could drive a meaningful de-rating.

Power is a tangible bottleneck. The concern is whether enough electricity will be available to energise planned US data-centre capacity by 2028, with knock-on risk for HBM/DRAM and optical suppliers. Jensen Huang also names power as the key constraint but sees it as solvable.

Funding is a major concern. Investors question how much chip demand depends on loss-making labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Debt-funded data-centre projects, higher borrowing costs and circular financing raise credit fears. Delayed infrastructure deals tied to credit uncertainty are the incremental data point worrying equity investors most.

Competition risks: new Meta and Google models, cheaper open-weight Chinese models and falling token prices pressure frontier-lab pricing power. Microsoft's Maia 300 and other hyperscaler custom silicon raise the prospect of a shift away from sole reliance on Nvidia and AMD. Stronger Chinese competition and easing supply tightness could weigh on DRAM and HBM pricing.

Offsetting catalysts named by the desk: accelerating total compute demand (token volume times compute intensity), strong enterprise, sovereign and neocloud orders, robust hyperscaler capex guidance into 2027-28, and confirmation that custom silicon is additive to high-end GPUs. The desk expects the sector to hold ahead of results, broadly supportive for hyperscalers and AI hardware. The Anthropic investor event in SF is another sentiment driver today, with focus on its ARR.

Payments preview for 3Q: the desk is broadly positive. Spending volumes are robust with September strong, regulatory and disruption risks are fading, agentic commerce is a growth driver, and the group is seen as insulated from higher rates, higher inflation and AI disruption. Stocks highlighted are V, MA, TOST and GLBE. More constructive on the setup for V, MA, PYPL, GLBE and RSKD, more cautious on FIS, FISV and FOUR.

Ofcom blocked Openreach from a nationwide GBP 9.50 monthly wholesale discount for new full-fibre customers but allowed a targeted GBP 50 one-off rebate in areas where BT competes with Virgin Media O2. This lets BT make more aggressive offers against VMO2. VMO2 criticised the decision.

Nexfibre's CEO challenged the CMA's provisional block of its GBP 2bn Netomnia acquisition, arguing CityFibre lacks the financial capacity to buy the business. He says the UK market supports only Openreach and one scaled challenger, and notes the government fast-tracked BT's emergency TalkTalk acquisition.

Vodafone asked Brussels to curb US vertically integrated groups such as SpaceX and Amazon. The appeal follows SpaceX's $8bn purchase of nationwide 800 MHz spectrum for direct-to-device services, which contributed to a telecom sell-off on 9 October. Vodafone, Orange, Telefonica and Deutsche Telekom plan a consortium bid for EU-reserved 2 GHz satellite spectrum in 2027, with AST SpaceMobile as interim partner to launch by 2029.

Creditors including Elliott, Sona and Arini sued Altice International in New York, alleging Drahi moved assets by designating Altice Portugal and Altice Caribbean (about 80% of group earnings) as unrestricted subsidiaries in late 2025. This follows a July 2026 default declaration on the EUR 8bn debt and a similar September suit against Optimum Communications.
AT&T agreed to sell AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2bn in cash at closing, expected to complete in Q1 2027. It will be held for sale from the Q3 2026 filing.

US trading was rangebound at index level with action under the surface. The GS Cycs v Defs pair traded lower in 6 of 7 sessions. Banks were mixed after earnings, with an early roll as rates rose, and the sector is likely a funding short for weakness in the AI trade. Tech squeezes (INFY, SaaS, HPQ) continued and the Quality factor stayed strong.

Floor activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale. HFs were moderate net buyers via macro products, while long-only flows skewed slightly to sale, driven by tech. Generalist/long-only outflows from Tech/AI/Memory continued, with dollars rotating out of the sector. Macro and non-traditional financials supply picked up. Volume was tracking -14% vs the 20-day average.

Derivatives: SPX closed essentially unchanged. NDX vol underperformed in gamma tenors. Skew steepened for most of the session on persistent demand for year-end downside. Customers bought 13k SPX 30Oct 7500 put spreads delta neutral. Tomorrow's SPX straddle is 0.52% ahead of CPI. The desk says it entered the session implying the lowest 1-day move of the year and this CPI straddle is one of the lowest for the event.

Publicis Q3 call: management reiterated 4.5-5% organic growth and pointed to the top end if macro stays stable. Sapient should return to modest growth in Q4, but it is only 13% of revenue so the impact on group growth is limited.

GS Research on US digital ads: Q3 trends are strong, with retail, travel and autos the strongest verticals and direct response outperforming brand. Agentic AI is the next battleground, and platforms with first-party data and closed-loop measurement, reinforcing Meta and Alphabet, are best positioned.

Other items: freenet buys the remaining minority in Exaring (waipu.tv) for about EUR 76m from cash. Wise named Barak Eilam Chair Designate to succeed David Wells in April 2027. Rightmove launched an AI Comparison Assistant built with Google Gemini.

tension_points.bull_case: Total compute demand (token volume times compute intensity) keeps accelerating despite competition and lower inference costs. ASML says customer demand exceeds capacity and is looking to add more. Hyperscaler capex remains robust into 2027-28 and custom silicon may be additive to high-end GPUs.
tension_points.bear_case: Power constraints, reliance on loss-making labs, circular financing and credit risk, falling token prices and custom silicon could cap high-end GPU spending. Crowded positioning with growth extending to 2027-28 means modest doubts could drive a meaningful de-rating.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Delayed infrastructure deals due to credit uncertainty and a power shortfall that leaves planned US data-centre capacity unenergised by 2028 would undermine the bull case. Evidence of accelerating compute demand and robust hyperscaler capex guidance would undermine the bear case.
